import sympy as sp

# Define the grid size
grid_size = 5

# Define the coordinates of the grid points
points = [(i, j) for i in range(grid_size) for j in range(grid_size)]

# Define the additional lines connecting the corners of the squares

    ((0, 1), (1, 1)), ((1, 1), (1, 0)), ((1, 0), (2, 0)),

    ((3, 0), (4, 0)), ((4, 0), (4, 5)), ((4, 0), (5, 0)),

    ((1, 4), (2, 4)), ((2, 4), (3, 4)), ((3, 4), (4, 4)),

    ((1, 2), (2, 2)), ((2, 2), (3, 2)), ((3, 2), (4, 2)),
    ((1, 3), (2, 3)), ((2, 3), (3, 3)), ((3, 3), (4, 3)),
    ((1, 4), (2, 4)), ((2, 4), (3, 4)), ((3, 4), (4, 4)),
    ((1, 5), (2, 5)), ((2, 5), (3, 5)), ((3, 5), (4, 5)),
    ((1, 1), (4, 1)), ((4, 1), (5, 1)), ((1, 2), (4, 2)),
    ((4, 2), (5, 2)), ((1, 3), (4, 3)), ((4, 3), (5, 3)),
    ((1, 4), (4, 4)), ((4, 4), (5, 4)), ((1, 5), (4, 5)),
    ((4, 5), (5, 5))
]

# Function to check if a set of points forms a square
def is_square(points):
    # Check if all points are valid and form a square
    if len(points) != 4:
        return False
    x1, y1 = points[0]
    x2, y2 = points[1]
    x3, y3 = points[2]
    x4, y4 = points[3]
    return (x1 == x2 or x1 == x3 or x1 == x4 or x2 == x3 or x2 == x4 or x3 == x4) and \
           (y1 == y2 or y1 == y3 or y1 == y4 or y2 == y3 or y2 == y4 or y3 == y4) and \
           (abs(x1 - x2) == abs(x3 - x4) or abs(y1 - y2) == abs(y3 - y4))

# Find all unique squares
unique_squares = set()
for i in range(len(points)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(points)):
        for k in range(j + 1, len(points)):
            for l in range(k + 1, len(points)):
                if is_square([points[i], points[j], points[k], points[l]]):
                    unique_squares.add(tuple(sorted([points[i], points[j], points[k], points[l]])))

# Count the number of unique squares
num_squares = len(unique_squares)
print(num_squares)
